items.title: Decide when and where to host
description: Choose a day and time that works for you, and book a room on campus that fits your expected number of guests.
If you will have 5+ guests, you'll want a room with a projector so not everyone is crowded around a laptop.
items.brainstormQuestion: How big of a room will I need? What is a good time to host so that students will be available and can easily attend?

inputs.label: Date and time for your event
Place on campus to host the event

items.title: Secure your fellow presenters
description: It's easier and more comfortable to host an event with others.
Think about other people you know who are interested in AI and use ChatGPT responsibly who might have a use case they would want to share. Invite them to present with you.
items.brainstormQuestion: Who else do you know that uses ChatGPT responsibly and would be excited to talk about their use?

inputs.label: People who might be interested in presenting

items.title: Create a slideshow
description: Events are easier to run when they are structured and have a clear flow.
It is best to create a slideshow.
Think about how you can introduce the flow of the event, give each presenter a slide, pose your guiding question, and add whatever else you want.
Consider using the template below to get started!

items.title: Invite people & promote
description: Use a tool like Lu.ma to build an event info and registration page.
Be sure to clearly explain the purpose, format, and what students will get out of it.
Include information about the 100 Chats project and you the host.
Start with personal connections: invite people you know, group chats you're a part of.
Then go wider: put up flyers, promote it at your club, and through normal campus channels.
items.brainstormQuestion: How might you promote the event and what ways will be most effective?

inputs.label: How you are going to promote the event

items.title: Plan the day-of logistics
description: If you're expecting 10+ people, it's worth having one or two trusted friends by your side.
Extra hands make the event run more smoothly—and make hosting feel lighter.
You might need help with: setting up the room/projector, greeting people, keeping time during show-and-tells, taking notes/photos, and anything else that helps you capture what you learn.
Think about any supplies you might need too.
items.brainstormQuestion: Would it be valuable to have some additional support and what materials might you need too?

inputs.label: Supplies you might need to secure
People you'll ask to help facilitate (optional)
